text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- The World Bank will extend some $800 million to Bulgaria over the next three years if a currency board is introduced and accompanied by structural reforms, a World Bank official told Balkan news agency.
-- The minimum monthly salary in Bulgaria is expected to rise to 6,303 levs from 5,500 levs effective from January, the cabinet 1997 draft budget figures show.
-- Bulgaria's private Security Insurance Company (SIC) raised its capital to 300 million levs from 100 million levs, a SIC senior official said.
-- Bulgaria's government is expecting the the dollar to trade at 320 levs in 1997 if a currency board is introduced in the country, draft 1997 budget figures showed.
-- Bulgaria's monthly consumer price inflation was 9.7 percent in November and the cumulative inflation for the first 11 months was 223.6 percent, National Statistics Institute figures showed.
-- The Sofia City court postponed untill March 19 ruling of an insolvency suit against Bulgaria's state Mineralbank and ordered an additional report on the bank's financial condition.

-- Bulgaria's trade ministry is expected to propose setting up a free trade zone with Poland and an agreement between the two countries is expected to be signed at the beginning of 1997, a Trade ministry official said.
